settings.context: Synthetic particle counts in independent equal-duration unit inspection windows; no validated physical process

rng.stream_policy: Instantiate once per named seed; no restart in replication loop; no seed search

ties.rule: rank=less+J; J uniform integer in [0,equal] inclusive

simultaneous_reference.scope: All ten bins across all six displayed panels

sbc.acceptance_gate: No histogram flatness or p-value gate

coverage.paired_mc_interval: normal approximation using sample SD of paired indicators / sqrt(R)

empirical_reference_screen.response: Investigate frozen outputs; never replace seeds

finite_reference.independent_exact_route: Monotone Poisson-CDF integer event inversion; no Gamma calls; actual-generator CDF/SF probability; neighboring integer checks

illustrations.selection: first 12, zero-based, for every generator/n; never selected by outcome

tolerances.curvature_step_scale: log coordinates or relative to positive rate mode
tolerances.boundary_review_policy: independent examination; never add tolerance to inclusion event

execution.authoritative_run: one fresh-kernel source notebook generated from current percent lab
execution.failed_attempts: retain real failures, nonfinite counts and denominators; do not preclaim zero

settings.amendment_policy: Immutable v1. New versioned amendment with reason and stale-output accounting for substantive repair; retain original and all attempts; no retuning for attractive findings.

simultaneous_reference.scope: All 60 displayed bins, conservative union bound

figures.alt: Resampling diagram: prior truths vary in SBC; truth is fixed for coverage; methods share each dataset.
Six rank histograms compare three algorithms on parameter and joint-likelihood quantities.
Coverage and mean width across sample sizes show concentration despite negative-binomial undercoverage.
Two fixed posterior illustrations and paired coverage contrasts show coordinate-dependent approximation error.

limitations: No human learning, accessibility or live tutor study.
SBC quantities are not universal correctness tests.
Wilson and paired normal intervals describe Monte Carlo error; paired intervals may be degenerate.
Asymptotic references are limits, not finite-n coverage.
